Then graveyards are exiled by Rest in Peace, so nothing comes back. So the opponent ends up with just a 6/6 flyer and loses Formidable Speaker. Libby has No More Lies (costs WU, needs 3 to pay) and Three Steps Ahead (costs U + 1U to counter). Libby has 4 untapped lands: Island, Hallowed Fountain, Rest in Peace (not a land), Seam Rip (not a land) - actually looking at the battlefield, tapped are: Hallowed Fountain, Meticulous Archive, Restless Anchorage, Floodfarm Verge. Untapped: Island, Hallowed Fountain (second one), and... that's only 2 untapped lands producing W and U. No More Lies costs WU - Libby can cast it with Island (U) + Hallowed Fountain (W). Three Steps Ahead counter mode costs 1UU - needs 3 mana. Libby only has 2 untapped lands. So only No More Lies is castable. A 6/6 flyer is a massive threat that will kill Libby in 3 attacks (Libby is at 16). Libby should counter this. Letting it resolve gives the opponent a dominant board position.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Bringer of the Last Gift, letting a 6/6 flyer resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast No More Lies targeting Bringer of the Last Gift. The opponent would need to pay 3 additional mana (likely tapped out after casting an 8-mana spell), so it would be countered and exiled. This prevents a 6/6 flying threat from hitting the battlefield.

annotations.description: Using Get Lost on Overlord of the Balemurk while Rest in Peace is already on the battlefield neutralizing its graveyard synergies. The Overlord still has time counters remaining before becoming a creature, so it's not an immediate threat. Get Lost gives the opponent two Map tokens, which provide card filtering/exploration value. With counterspells (No More Lies, Three Steps Ahead) in hand, Libby could afford to wait and use Get Lost on a more threatening permanent later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Get Lost targeting Overlord of the Balemurk at end of turn, giving opponent two Map tokens
annotations.betterLine: Hold Get Lost for a higher-value target. The Overlord is partially neutralized by Rest in Peace and won't become a creature for several turns. Counterspells in hand can handle future threats. Alternatively, if concerned about Overlord, wait until closer to when it would become a creature to assess whether removal is still needed.

annotations.description: Get Lost is on the stack targeting one of Libby's critical enchantments (Rest in Peace or Seam Rip). Rest in Peace is shutting down the opponent's entire graveyard strategy (Overlord of the Balemurk, Bringer of the Last Gift). The opponent has all lands tapped, meaning No More Lies would be an unconditional counter since they can't pay {3}.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Get Lost, allowing the opponent to destroy a key enchantment.
annotations.betterLine: Counter Get Lost with No More Lies (guaranteed to resolve since opponent has no mana to pay the {3} tax) to protect Rest in Peace or Seam Rip.

annotations.description: Wistfulness can target and exile Rest in Peace (if {G}{G} was spent), which is the linchpin enchantment keeping the opponent's graveyard strategy in check. Letting it resolve risks losing the most important card on Libby's board against this Overlord of the Balemurk / Bringer of the Last Gift deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Wistfulness, letting it resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast No More Lies targeting Wistfulness. Even if the opponent can pay {3}, it forces them to tap out completely. If they can't pay, Rest in Peace is saved. The risk of losing Rest in Peace is too high to not attempt the counter.

annotations.description: Discarded Harvester of Misery (a castable 5/4 menace for 5 mana) to keep Sunderflock, which costs 9 mana with no Elemental cost reduction available. While Sunderflock's mass bounce is powerful, it requires exactly 9 mana and the opponent has Rest in Peace and Seam Rip (enchantments) that won't be bounced. Harvester provides an immediate castable threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Harvester of Misery, keeping Sunderflock and Willowrush Verge
annotations.betterLine: Discard Sunderflock instead, keeping Harvester of Misery as a castable 5/4 menace threat and Willowrush Verge for the land drop

annotations.description: Used a Map Token instead of playing Willowrush Verge. With Rest in Peace on the opponent's board, the Map Token's surveil effect is weakened (cards go to exile instead of graveyard). More importantly, playing Willowrush Verge would bring Timmy to 9 lands, enabling casting Sunderflock (which costs 9 with no Elementals in play) next turn. Delaying the land drop delays the ability to cast their best card.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Map Token instead of playing Willowrush Verge
annotations.betterLine: Play Willowrush Verge first to reach 9 lands, then potentially use Map Token with remaining mana, enabling Sunderflock cast on the following turn.

annotations.description: Playing Meticulous Archive (enters tapped) instead of Island (enters untapped) when wanting to hold up countermagic (No More Lies + Three Steps Ahead). While surveil 1 provides some deck filtering, Rest in Peace is on the battlefield, meaning any card surveilled to the graveyard gets exiled instead, significantly reducing the value. With Overlord of the Balemurk counting down time counters, maximizing available mana for counterspells is important.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Meticulous Archive as the land drop (enters tapped, surveil diminished by Rest in Peace)
annotations.betterLine: Play Island (enters untapped for free) to maximize available mana for holding up countermagic, saving Meticulous Archive for a less critical turn

annotations.description: Grok4F Libby declined to counter Day of Judgment while having both No More Lies and Three Steps Ahead available. Rest in Peace is on the battlefield, which means the opponent's graveyard is exiled and their Overlord of the Balemurk's mill/recursion strategy is neutered. However, Restless Anchorage is Libby's primary win condition as a creature land, and Day of Judgment doesn't destroy it (it's not currently a creature). Looking more carefully: Libby has no creatures on board - Seam Rip is an enchantment exiling something, Rest in Peace is an enchantment, and Restless Anchorage is a land. The opponent has Overlord of the Balemurk as a non-creature enchantment (it was cast with Impending, so it still has time counters and isn't a creature yet). So Day of Judgment actually destroys nothing on either side currently. In that case, letting it resolve is correct since it's a wasted spell by the opponent. Wait - let me reconsider. Overlord of the Balemurk with Impending means it's not a creature yet. Libby has no creatures. Day of Judgment would destroy zero creatures. Letting it resolve wastes the opponent's card and preserves Libby's counterspells for actual threats. This is actually the correct play.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Day of Judgment
annotations.betterLine: Actually, letting Day of Judgment resolve was correct since there are no creatures on the battlefield to destroy - the Overlord is still in impending mode (enchantment only) and Libby has no creatures.

annotations.description: Cast Sunderflock before playing a land. With only 8 lands and Sunderflock costing 9 mana (no Elementals to reduce cost), the correct sequence is to play Willowrush Verge first (enters untapped due to controlling Forests/Islands), giving 9 lands to properly cast Sunderflock. Additionally, playing the land first preserves the land drop in case Sunderflock gets countered (opponent has W+U open for No More Lies).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sunderflock with only 8 lands before making a land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Willowrush Verge first to reach 9 lands, then cast Sunderflock. This ensures proper mana and preserves the land drop if the spell is countered.

annotations.description: Playing Watery Grave over Willowrush Verge when Timmy already has abundant U/B sources. Watery Grave either costs 2 life (at 12 life against a deck with Restless Anchorage pressure) or enters tapped, while Willowrush Verge enters untapped for free and produces U or G (G enabled by existing Islands). With only Requiting Hex in hand needing B mana they already have plenty of, there's no reason to prioritize Watery Grave.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Watery Grave as land for turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Willowrush Verge (enters untapped for free), save Watery Grave for a future turn when the dual land flexibility might matter more or life total is less pressured

annotations.actionTaken: Cast Aang's Iceberg with no meaningful target during precombat main
annotations.betterLine: Activate Restless Anchorage for {1}{W}{U} to create a 2/3 flyer, attack for 2 damage against tapped-out opponent, create a Map token, then hold up remaining mana for countermagic (No More Lies or Three Steps Ahead)

annotations.description: Cast Superior Spider-Man before playing Willowrush Verge. Land should be played first for correct sequencing, even though the extra mana isn't needed for this specific spell. Additionally, Superior Spider-Man's Mind Swap ability is completely blanked by the opponent's Rest in Peace (all graveyards are exiled), making it just a vanilla 4/4 - though with only these two cards in hand, casting it is still the best available play.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Superior Spider-Man before playing the land, into a Rest in Peace that blanks its copy ability.
annotations.betterLine: Play Willowrush Verge first, then cast Superior Spider-Man. The card is still the best available play given the limited hand, but sequencing land first is strictly better.

annotations.description: Cast Get Lost with no meaningful opposing targets on the board. The opponent has only lands in play - no creatures, enchantments, or planeswalkers to destroy. The only valid targets would be Libby's own Rest in Peace or Seam Rip, which is counterproductive and gives the opponent two Map tokens for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Get Lost with no good targets on the opponent's board
annotations.betterLine: Play Island, then pass the turn holding up No More Lies and Three Steps Ahead as countermagic for when the opponent tries to deploy threats.

annotations.description: Get Lost is on the stack, almost certainly targeting Rest in Peace, which is the key hate piece shutting down the opponent's entire graveyard-based strategy (Overlord of the Balemurk recursion, etc.). Libby has both No More Lies and Three Steps Ahead in hand with mana available to cast either, but chose not to counter.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Get Lost, allowing it to resolve and likely destroy Rest in Peace, giving the opponent two Map tokens as well.
annotations.betterLine: Counter Get Lost with No More Lies (WU, cheap and efficient) to protect Rest in Peace and maintain the graveyard lockout against the opponent's graveyard-centric deck.

annotations.description: Cast Aang's Iceberg when the opponent has no nonland permanents on the battlefield, wasting 3 mana and a card for no meaningful effect. Three Steps Ahead in draw mode would have generated card advantage while still leaving mana to hold up No More Lies.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Aang's Iceberg with no meaningful targets on the opponent's board
annotations.betterLine: Cast Three Steps Ahead in draw mode (3 mana) to draw 2 cards and discard 1, then hold up remaining mana for No More Lies as counterplay

annotations.description: Grok4F Libby chose to cast Aang's Iceberg (which exiles a nonland permanent — but the opponent has none on the battlefield) instead of No More Lies to counter Three Steps Ahead on the stack. The opponent had only 2 untapped mana remaining after casting Three Steps Ahead, so they couldn't pay the {3} tax from No More Lies, meaning it would have been a hard counter. Instead, Three Steps Ahead resolves (likely drawing 2 cards) and Aang's Iceberg accomplishes nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Aang's Iceberg, which has no meaningful target and doesn't interact with Three Steps Ahead on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Cast No More Lies to counter Three Steps Ahead. The opponent cannot pay {3} with only 2 untapped lands, so it would be a hard counter for just WU.

annotations.description: Naming 'Human' on Cavern of Souls when the deck's most impactful creatures appear to be non-Human types. annotations.betterLine: Consider naming 'Elemental' (for Sunderflock/Formidable Speaker) or 'Avatar' (for Overlord of the Balemurk) depending on which threats are most important to resolve against the control deck

annotations.description: Grok4F Libby cast Stock Up (a sorcery costing 2U) during their main phase before playing their Plains land drop. By playing Plains first, they would have had 9 lands available instead of 8, which matters for leaving up countermagic (No More Lies costs WU) after casting their draw spell. With 8 lands and Stock Up costing 3, they have 5 mana remaining - enough for No More Lies. However, if they had played Plains first, they could have cast Consult the Star Charts (kicked for 1U + 1U = 4 mana total) instead with the benefit of looking at 9 cards and getting 2, which would likely be superior to Stock Up's look-at-5-get-2, while still leaving 5 mana open for countermagic. Additionally, the general principle of playing lands before spells avoids information loss.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Stock Up before playing Plains from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains first, then either cast Stock Up with more mana remaining, or cast kicked Consult the Star Charts (looking at 9 cards instead of 5 for the same number of cards drawn) while still leaving up No More Lies mana

annotations.description: With no opponent creatures on board, declining to activate Restless Anchorage as a 2/3 flyer to attack for 2 damage misses free pressure. With 8 lands available, activating for {1}{W}{U} still leaves 5 lands untapped - enough to hold up No More Lies ({W}{U}) or Tishana's Tidebinder ({2}{U}) for protection. At 2 life vs 10 life, every point of damage matters to close out the game before the opponent draws threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Restless Anchorage during combat, not attacking.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Restless Anchorage for {1}{W}{U} to make it a 2/3 flyer, attack for 2 damage (and create a Map token), while keeping enough mana open for countermagic.

annotations.description: Cast Day of Judgment with zero creatures on the entire battlefield. The spell destroys nothing and is completely wasted. At 2 life with limited cards in hand, throwing away a board wipe that could have been critical later is devastating.

annotations.betterLine: Play Plains for the land drop, then pass the turn holding up No More Lies (WU counter) and Tishana's Tidebinder (flash creature with ability counter). This preserves the board wipe for when the opponent actually deploys threats.

annotations.description: At 2 life with the opponent at 8, Grok4F Libby needs a win condition. Restless Anchorage is a flying creature land that can attack for 2 and create Map tokens - it's the primary way a control deck closes games. With 8 lands already in play, they have more than enough untapped mana to hold up No More Lies (WU), Spell Snare (U), and Tidebinder (2U) even with Restless Anchorage entering tapped. Plains provides redundant mana with no strategic upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains, a basic land with no additional utility.
annotations.betterLine: Play Restless Anchorage to establish a win condition. Even entering tapped, the existing 8 lands provide sufficient mana for all counterspells in hand. The creature land would allow attacking for 2 flying damage per turn to close out the game.

annotations.description: Casting Tishana's Tidebinder in precombat main phase before playing the Restless Anchorage land. Lands should be played before spells as a general sequencing principle - it's free and keeps options open. Additionally, Tidebinder has flash and could be held up alongside counterspells to react to opponent's plays, which is especially relevant at 2 life where every decision matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tishana's Tidebinder before playing Restless Anchorage land
annotations.betterLine: Play Restless Anchorage first, then consider whether to deploy Tidebinder now or hold it with flash alongside No More Lies and Spell Snare for the opponent's turn, maintaining maximum flexibility at 2 life

annotations.description: At 2 life with Tishana's Tidebinder (3/2 flash) on the stack, activating Restless Anchorage now makes it a creature only until end of THIS turn - it won't be available as a blocker during the opponent's next combat. Meanwhile, No More Lies would either counter the Tidebinder (if opponent can't pay 3) or at minimum tax 3 mana from the opponent. Letting a 3/2 resolve when at 2 life without attempting to counter it is potentially game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Restless Anchorage to become a 2/3 creature until end of turn (useless since it's Libby's turn and won't persist to block)
annotations.betterLine: Cast No More Lies targeting Tishana's Tidebinder to either counter it or force the opponent to pay 3 additional mana, preserving Restless Anchorage activation for blocking on the opponent's combat step

annotations.description: GPT4om Timmy used Awaken the Honored Dead's Chapter I destroy ability to target itself, completely wasting the card for no effect. The opponent is at 2 life and has Rest in Peace (which shuts down graveyard strategies), Seam Rip (which is exiling one of Timmy's permanents), and Tishana's Tidebinder on the battlefield. Any of these would have been a meaningful target. Rest in Peace is particularly devastating as it exiles all cards that would go to graveyards, neutering Timmy's entire game plan. Tishana's Tidebinder is a 3/2 creature that could block or attack. Seam Rip is exiling something. Instead, Timmy destroyed their own saga for zero value.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Awaken the Honored Dead (itself) with its own Chapter I destroy ability, destroying it for no benefit.
annotations.betterLine: Destroy Rest in Peace to re-enable graveyard strategies, or destroy Tishana's Tidebinder to remove a creature threat, or destroy Seam Rip to get back the exiled permanent. With the opponent at 2 life, removing Tidebinder (a blocker/attacker) or Rest in Peace (to unlock graveyard recursion for future turns) would have been far superior.

annotations.description: Grok4F Libby is at 2 life and their opponent cast Bitter Triumph targeting Tishana's Tidebinder. By not countering Bitter Triumph, Libby loses Tishana's Tidebinder, which was likely locking down something important (possibly Overlord of the Balemurk). At 2 life with the opponent also at 2, losing a key creature and potentially unlocking an opponent's threat is devastating. Either Spell Snare (free, costs only {U}) or No More Lies would have saved the Tidebinder.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Bitter Triumph, allowing Tishana's Tidebinder to be destroyed.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Spell Snare targeting Bitter Triumph (mana value 2) to counter it and keep Tishana's Tidebinder alive.
